comments.name: Jack Reynolds, Ph.D.
comments.text:
Learn from my mistake. This is from an email from @twin_labs (https://t.co/7pLOzYu0Ri) after their model consumed credits NOT doing what was asked of it.

"Your run on April 23 did complete and produced 225 Google Docs, but you're right that many of the Stage 4 copy edit documents came out empty or near-empty. What happened is that the LLM (the AI model) returned empty or truncated content for a significant number of those calls. . . . One of your runs got caught in a cycle where the agent kept wiping its database and restarting the pipeline from scratch instead of progressing forward. Our system detected this and stopped the run after about 35 minutes, but it still consumed 470 credits before being caught. . . . After a thorough investigation, the issues you experienced -- the empty files and the stuck loop -- were caused by the AI model's decisions and the pipeline design (that was designed by @twin_labs, not me). . . . [T]he platform executed every request correctly. Because of this, these issues don't qualify for a credit refund . . ."

Do not use this company,@twin_labs.

comments.text: ⟁108 The "AI company builder" category is one of the biggest unlocks of 2026. Most people still think building an AI company means writing code. comments.name: AI Builder🚀
comments.text: @hugomercierooo The agent deployment model is interesting but the real question is what happens when those 100K agents hit real-world edge cases. Most AI products look great in beta. The test is production scale. Curious to see how Twin's agents handle multi-step reasoning under load.

comments.name: WeGo2Mars
comments.text: @hugomercierooo building the same thing for gold futures. self-learning trading system that adapts to regime. the "one-person hedge fund" framing is exactly right — the goal is removing the human from execution, not from thinking

comments.name: CEDX
comments.text: @hugomercierooo Finance back-office is the big one. PE firms especially — LP reporting, month-end close, compliance reviews — still 90% manual spreadsheets. AI finally has enough context to handle it properly. The ROI is immediate and obvious once you show them.

comments.name: Aniket Tapre
comments.text: @hugomercierooo 100K agents deployed is strong traction. The AI company builder space is heating up fast. On the workflow orchestration side, Helium (https://t.co/QGTGLDwqkr) takes a similar no-setup approach but focuses on automating complex business processes through conversation.

comments.name: Spocky Magic AI
comments.text: We're living this at SpockyMagicAI — a 100% AI-driven company where autonomous systems handle everything from marketing to strategy. The future isn't AI replacing humans at existing companies. It's entirely new company structures built AI-first from day one. Who else is building AI-native?

comments.name: ADI
comments.text: @hugomercierooo @hugomercierooo Context isolation between twin agents matters when you're specifically looking for divergent answers — shared context just produces consensus. The value is in the gap between their outputs, not the average. Do you score the disagreements?
